details.biography:
The Broken Anvil · Level 1 - The Recruits · Seat 5, Spare

A young woman in a red hood with a longbow nearly as tall as she is, and a habit of climbing anything that gives a good view. Bright, eager and stubborn; she counts her arrows twice and her blessings once. She learned volley drill on the walls of Westfront Fort and grew up on the war stories of her uncle Marten Halloway, a veteran she is determined to impress.

Tonight: Uncle Marten will hear how tonight went, so it had better go well.

In a fight

Move at least 10ft, then shoot for Advantage on your first arrow; Steady Aim lets you shoot into a melee without penalty. Save Fire Arrows for spilled oil, rope bridges and anything that matters. Shoot what a friend just hit: your first arrow on it ignores its resistances (Volley Timing).
details.backgroundStory:
Abilities

Running Shot. If you moved at least 10ft this turn before attacking with a bow, Advantage on your first bow attack that turn. Standing still gives nothing.

Arrow Repertoire: Fire and Rope. Fire Arrow: +1d6 fire on a hit, and it can set flammable things alight. Rope Arrow: trails a thin line up to 60ft and anchors on a solid hit; it can be climbed. Craft up to 4 special arrows a day (Dex +3, level 1) when you have materials, and carry no more than 4. You start with 3 Fire and 1 Rope.

Bent Path. Your first shot each round ignores the Disadvantage from Half Cover and reduces a shield's AC bonus by 2. Full Cover still blocks it.

Fletcher's Craft (Intelligence). Repair or craft bows, strings and arrows from what is to hand, and identify odd or trapped arrows.

Volley Timing (kit). Your first bow hit each round on a creature an ally hit with a ranged attack since your last turn ignores its resistances.

Sentry's Patience (kit). Advantage on Perception checks on watch or sentry duty.

Human. Speed 30ft, no darkvision. Knack: Spotting, with Advantage on Wisdom checks to notice things (not an NWP slot). Trained in two martial weapons of your choice (longsword and spear, not carried).

Steady Aim (1st, Specialist). No Disadvantage on ranged attacks against a target in melee with an ally.

Perceptive Grit (1st, General, Human bonus feat). +1 Wisdom (included). Advantage on Perception checks to avoid being surprised or ambushed.

Armour Class on the sheet: 10 + 2 (Leather Armour, Light) + 3 (Dex, full) = 15

Class Abilities

1st Level

Running Shot

  • Effect: If you moved at least 10ft this turn before attacking with a bow, gain advantage on your first bow attack roll that turn.

Fletcher's Craft (Intelligence)

  • Effect: Repair or craft bows, strings, and arrows from available materials. Also governs identifying nonstandard or trapped arrows found in the field.

Arrow Repertoire

  • Effect: You know two special arrow types from the list below, chosen at character creation.
  • Each day you can craft special arrows up to your daily pool, Dexterity modifier + Archer level (minimum 1), if you have the materials.
  • Unused arrows keep from day to day.
  • Carry limit: You can never carry more crafted arrows than your daily pool. Once you hold that many, you can't craft more until you use some.
  • Fire Arrow: +1d6 fire damage on hit; can ignite flammable material
  • Whistling Arrow: deals no damage, but is audible up to 500ft and can be used as a signal; a creature unfamiliar with the sound makes a Will save against your Class Save DC or is Shaken for 1 round
  • Rope Arrow: trails a thin line up to 60ft, anchors on a solid hit; can be climbed
  • Broadhead Arrow: has the Armour Piercing trait, no other bonus
  • From 3rd level: learn one additional arrow type from the list.
  • From 15th level: learn a fourth arrow type. Daily crafted arrow pool doubles.

Bent Path

  • Effect: Your first shot each round curves around cover and shields. Half Cover doesn't give you Disadvantage on it, and the target's shield adds 2 less to its AC.
  • 10th level: it can also curve around Full Cover: you can target a creature behind it, with Disadvantage. It ignores the target's shield entirely, magic included.
  • 11th level: it applies to every shot you make, not just the first each round

2nd Level

Bow Mastery

  • Effect: You deal +1 damage with bows, rising to +2 at 6th level, +3 at 12th and +4 at 18th.

3rd Level

Perfect Loose

  • Effect: Once per day, declare before rolling. The next shot deals maximum damage regardless of dice result. If part of a Twin Nock attack, applies to one arrow of the volley.

4th Level

Called Shot (Archer)

  • Effect: You can make Called Shots (see Combat Manoeuvres in The Arneyan Codex); from 10th level they don't take the Disadvantage.

5th Level

Twin Nock

  • Effect: Fire two arrows in place of the one attack your action gives you.
  • Extra Attack, an off-hand weapon and Flowing Strikes add nothing to it: a Twin Nock is two arrows (three from 17th) and no more.
  • The second arrow is rolled with Disadvantage until 10th level, and from 10th level there is no penalty.
  • Can split between two targets within range, or fire both at the same target.
  • Each arrow gets your Bow Mastery bonus.
  • Cannot combine with Running Shot's advantage on the same turn until 13th level (see Loosed in Passing): until then, choose one or the other each turn: move-and-shoot for advantage, or plant your feet for two arrows.

6th Level

Longshot

  • Effect: Double the range of your bows, and you take no penalty at long range.

7th Level

Skirmish

  • Effect: On a turn you make a bow attack, your speed increases by 10ft, and creatures you shot this turn can't make Attacks of Opportunity against you.

8th Level

Hail of Arrows

  • Effect: Once per encounter, as your action, make one bow attack against every creature in a 15ft radius within long range (Longshot's range), rolling damage separately for each.
  • 12th level: a 20ft radius
  • 17th level: a 30ft radius, and a second use per encounter

9th Level

Pinning Shot

  • Effect: On a hit against a creature next to a wall, tree, mast or the ground (if Prone), it makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC or is Restrained until it spends an action to pull the arrow free.

11th Level

Seeker

  • Effect: You add your Wisdom modifier (minimum 0) to bow damage.

13th Level

Loosed in Passing

  • Effect: Twin Nock and Running Shot no longer conflict: fire both arrows while moving and still gain Running Shot's advantage.

15th Level

Dexterity Bonus

  • Effect: Permanent +1 Dexterity.

17th Level

Never Still

  • Effect: Running Shot's advantage now applies even if you moved less than 10ft, as long as you moved at all this turn. Additionally, Twin Nock becomes three arrows instead of two, splittable among up to three targets, each still carrying your Bow Mastery bonus.

20th Level

Perfect Loose (Improved)

  • Effect: Perfect Loose also applies Bent Path's 10th-level effect, and it covers every arrow of a Twin Nock.

Renown: Bowyers' Lodge

  • Effect: You may found a bowyers' lodge (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 archers and a fletcher join it. While you hold it, your daily arrow pool doubles again whenever you rest at the lodge.

24th Level

The Arrow Finds Its Mark

  • Effect: Once per encounter, make a single ranged attack against any target you have line of sight to, regardless of range, cover, or obstruction: the shot arcs and curves as needed to arrive. No distance penalty, Half and Full Cover do not hinder it, and this attack cannot be a called shot (the trick is in the path, not the placement).

Kits: Archer Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Archer folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Kit at character creation. Your kit defines the terrain, tradition, and context that shaped your relationship with the bow.

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision None • +1 / +1 to any two attributes of choice, no penalty

Traits

  • Choose one skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills. It keeps its Advantage if you later train or master the skill.
  • Gains an additional Feat from the General Path (The Survivors) at 1st level, on top of their normal 1st-level Feat choice. It follows the usual prerequisites, and can't be a Feat you already have.
  • Weapon training: any two martial weapons of choice.
  • Armour training: light, medium.
